title: The integer indices in an independent root string form an interval
statement: Let $I$ be finite, let $M,N$ be vector spaces over the field $\mathbf Q$ [def-weil-field], and let $P:\mathrm{RootPairing}\ I\ \mathbf Q\ M\ N$ be a crystallographic root pairing in the Mathlib sense: injective root and coroot families with a perfect bilinear pairing, root-coroot value $2$, simultaneous reflection permutations, and integral root-coroot pairings. Write $a_i=P.\mathrm{root}(i)$. Let $i,j\in I$ with $a_i,a_j$ linearly independent over $\mathbf Q$. Put $p=P.\mathrm{chainBotCoeff}(i,j)$ and $q=P.\mathrm{chainTopCoeff}(i,j)$, the largest nonnegative integers with $a_j-pa_i$ and $a_j+qa_i$ roots, respectively. Then for every integer $z$, $$a_j+za_i\in\operatorname{range}(P.\mathrm{root})\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad -p\le z\le q.$$
